summary: FixLangevinKokkos's constructor re-allocates ratio[] and resets every entry to 1.0 after the base constructor already stored the user's 'scale' keyword values, so 'fix langevin/kk ... scale <type> <value>' is silently ignored.
failure_scenario: 'fix f all langevin/kk 300 300 100 12345 scale 2 10.0' damps type-2 atoms with ratio 1.0 instead of 10.0; the /kk run gives a different (wrong) trajectory and temperature from the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Copy the base-class ratio values into the new dual view instead of overwriting them: save the old ratio pointer before 'delete[] ratio', copy old_ratio[i] into the new array for i=1..ntypes, then modify_host().

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::post_force() calls the non-virtual host-only FixLangevin::omega_thermostat() instead of the device version, with no sync/modified bookkeeping, so 'fix langevin/kk ... omega yes' updates only a stale host torque array while the device kernel omega_thermostat_kokkos() is dead code.
failure_scenario: GPU run with granular particles: 'fix 1 all langevin/kk 300 300 100 4321 omega yes'.  Pair style leaves torque device-current; the host loop reads a stale host torque/omega and writes the host copy, which is never claimed, so the device integrator (fix nve/sphere/kk) never sees the rotational drag or random torque -- the rotational thermostat is silently a no-op (and the host arrays it read are garbage).
suggested_fix: Rename FixLangevinKokkos::omega_thermostat_kokkos() to omega_thermostat() (and declare FixLangevin::omega_thermostat() virtual), so the KOKKOS device kernel is the one invoked from post_force().

summary: zero_force_item() subtracts the mean random force from f only, not from d_flangevin, so with 'zero yes tally yes' the tallied Langevin energy uses an uncorrected force (the CPU version corrects both).
failure_scenario: 'fix f all langevin/kk 300 300 100 999 zero yes tally yes' -- f_f (the cumulative energy transferred to the reservoir, used in ecouple/thermo output and for energy conservation checks) differs from the equivalent non-kk run by the omitted -fsumall*v term at every step.
suggested_fix: In zero_force_item(), also subtract d_fsumall from d_flangevin(i,*) when the tally array is active (add a template flag, mirroring Tp_TALLY in the CPU code).

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::setup() unconditionally calls post_force(vflag), dropping the r-RESPA branch of the base setup() and without erroring out on respa the way every other KOKKOS fix does.
failure_scenario: 'run_style respa 2 2' plus 'fix f all langevin/kk ...': at setup the Langevin force is added to atom->f without copy_flevel_f/copy_f_flevel, so the outer-level respa force array does not contain it and the first steps of the run use a different force than the non-kk build.
suggested_fix: Either replicate the base setup()'s respa branch, or add the standard 'Cannot (yet) use respa with fix langevin/kk' error in FixLangevinKokkos::init().

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::end_of_step() marks V_MASK and k_lv as device-modified although it only reads v and never touches lv.
failure_scenario: Spurious device->host copies of v every step; and if lv were ever registered for atom callbacks (grow_arrays/copy_arrays are currently dead code because fix langevin registers no Atom::GROW callback), a copy_arrays() followed by end_of_step() would hit Kokkos::abort on a GPU build.
suggested_fix: Delete both statements: end_of_step() writes nothing.  Consider removing the vestigial lv/franprev/end_of_step_item code entirely now that the gjf option has been removed from fix langevin.

summary: The KOKKOS constructor deletes and re-creates ratio[] and then resets every entry to 1.0 AFTER the base constructor already stored the user's 'scale <type> <value>' values, so the scale keyword is silently ignored under -sf kk.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/fix_langevin.cpp:87-91 allocates and defaults ratio, :119 stores the user value; src/KOKKOS/fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:60-74 re-creates it and re-defaults every entry).

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::end_of_step claims device writes (atomKK->modified(V_MASK) and k_lv.modify<DeviceType>()) that the launched kernel never performs.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:757-766: `atomKK->sync(execution_space,V_MASK | MASK_MASK); k_flangevin.template sync<DeviceType>(); if (tallyflag) { FixLangevinKokkosTallyEnergyFunctor<DeviceType> tally_functor(this); Kokkos::parallel_reduce(nlocal,tally_functor,energy_onestep); } atomKK->modified(execution_space,V_MASK); k_lv.template modify<DeviceType>();`.  The only kernel launched is TallyEnergyFunctor, whose body is compute_energy_item() (line 728), a pure reduction that writes nothing.  end_of_step_item()/end_of_step_rmass_item() (lines 774, 794), the only functions that write `v` and `d_lv`, are reached solely through FixLangevinKokkosEndOfStepFunctor (fix_langevin_kokkos.h:260-275) which is never instantiated anywhere in the .cpp.  The CPU base FixLangevin::end_of_step (src/fix_langevin.cpp) likewise only accumulates `energy_onestep`.
failure_scenario: The bogus `k_lv.modify<DeviceType>()` makes the never-written device buffer authoritative; the next FixLangevinKokkos::copy_arrays (line 820) starts with `k_lv.sync_host()`, which then overwrites the host `lv` array with that untouched device buffer.  The redundant `atomKK->modified(execution_space,V_MASK)` additionally forces a full velocity copy back every step.
suggested_fix: Drop both claims from end_of_step(), or instantiate FixLangevinKokkosEndOfStepFunctor if the half-step-velocity swap is actually meant to run; also remove the dead end_of_step_item()/end_of_step_rmass_item()/functor if it is not.

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() gates on `r < d_cutsq(itype,jtype)`, comparing a distance against a SQUARED cutoff, and runs the knot search before the gate, so calls with r past the cutoff walk off the end of d_n2b_knot and evaluate the spline with a bogus index.
failure_scenario: `pair_style uf3 2` (single_enable stays 1, see src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:122-125) plus `pair_write 1 1 500 r 0.5 8.0 out.txt`: for every r >= cut the while-loop indexes d_n2b_knot past its last knot (extent max_num_knots_2b), reading out of bounds and/or looping until it happens to find a larger value, then constants_2b(...) is read at that bogus start_index; uf3/kk returns garbage (or crashes) where plain uf3 returns 0.
suggested_fix: Move the knot search inside the guard and compare rsq against d_cutsq (or r against cut[itype][jtype]), exactly as PairUF3::single does.

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() does not scale the returned force by factor_lj, so special-bond scaled pairs get an unscaled force while the energy is scaled.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1648 `fforce = static_cast<double>(dnconstants_2b(interaction_id, start_index - 1, 0));` ... line 1659 `return factor_lj * value;` -- the CPU base src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:1857 does `fforce = factor_lj * force_2b;` before `return factor_lj * value;` (line 1878).
failure_scenario: Any caller of single() with factor_lj != 1 (special_bonds scaling, e.g. `compute group/group` style callers or a tabulation over bonded pairs) gets fforce too large by 1/factor_lj from uf3/kk while plain uf3 returns the scaled value.
suggested_fix: Multiply the accumulated fforce by factor_lj, matching PairUF3::single.

summary: `kokkosable = 1;` is commented out in the PairUF3Kokkos constructor, so VerletKokkos treats uf3/kk as a non-KOKKOS pair style and turns on auto_sync for the whole pair compute.
failure_scenario: Every uf3/kk step forces a full host/device round trip of x/f/energy/virial through auto_sync, negating the point of the port; also src/force.cpp:208's kokkosable sanity check is bypassed.
suggested_fix: Uncomment `kokkosable = 1;` (and verify the style really keeps its data device-resident) or document why it must stay off.

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() runs the knot search BEFORE any cutoff guard and then gates on 'r < d_cutsq(itype,jtype)', comparing a distance against a squared cutoff. For r beyond the cutoff the while loop walks off the end of d_n2b_knot, and the admitted range extends to cut^2.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1617-1622 vs src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:1845-1846, which guards first with 'if (r < cut[itype][jtype])' and only then looks up the starting knot index).

summary: TagPairVashishtaComputeFullB indexes the short 3-body neighbor list with the loop counter `jj` (a slot index inside i's own list) instead of the neighbor atom id `j`, so the kernel walks the neighbor list of an unrelated atom when adding the leg force on i.
failure_scenario: `pair_style vashishta/kk` with `-pk kokkos neigh full` (the default on a GPU build): FullA supplies only the centre-atom part of each 3-body term and FullB is supposed to add the leg force on i from triplets centred on its neighbours j. With the wrong index, FullB evaluates threebody() for triplets (j; i, k) where k comes from an unrelated atom's list, so rsq2 = |x(k)-x(j)|^2 is arbitrary; the resulting forces are wrong and non-conservative (and can be enormous when |x(k)-x(j)| happens to fall just outside r0, where exp(gamma/(r-r0)) blows up).
suggested_fix: Use `d_numneigh_short_3body[j]` and `d_neighbors_short_3body(j,kk)`. Note the same code is present in stanmoore1/lammps develop, so this looks like a latent upstream defect (the FULL path is not exercised by the CPU-only CI, which runs neighflag=HALF).

summary: In TagPairVashishtaComputeFullB the cheap threebodyj() variant is chosen on vflag_atom alone, so when eflag_atom is on but vflag_atom is off the three-body energy is never computed and ev_tally3_atom() adds a hard zero to d_eatom.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_vashishta_kokkos.cpp:480 `KK_FLOAT evdwl = 0.0;` ... 525-530 `if (vflag_atom)
          threebody(d_params[jiparam],...,eflag,evdwl);
        else
          threebodyj(d_params[jiparam],...,fj);` (threebodyj, line 744, has no eng argument and never writes evdwl) ... 536-537 `if (EVFLAG)
          if (vflag_atom || eflag_atom) ev_tally3_atom(ev,i,evdwl,0.0,fj,fk,delr1,delr2);`, and ev_tally3_atom (line 953) does `epairthird = THIRD*(evdwl+ecoul); d_eatom[i] += epairthird;`. In the FULL path ev_tally3 only credits the centre atom (`if (NEIGHFLAG != FULL)` guards j and k at lines 892-895), so the two leg thirds must come from FullB.
failure_scenario: `pair_style vashishta/kk` + `-pk kokkos neigh full` + `compute pe/atom` without any per-atom stress: every atom gets only the 1/3 of each three-body energy for triplets it centres, losing the 2/3 it should receive as a leg; the per-atom energies no longer sum to the (correct) global eng_vdwl.
suggested_fix: Select threebody() when `vflag_atom || eflag_atom` (and keep threebodyj() only for the no-tally case), or give threebodyj an energy output.

summary: TagPairVashishtaComputeFullB indexes the short 3-body neighbour list with the slot counter jj instead of the neighbour atom j: 'const int j_jnum = d_numneigh_short_3body[jj];' and 'int k = d_neighbors_short_3body(jj,kk);'. jj only runs over 0..jnum-1, so the kernel walks the 3-body lists of atoms 0,1,2,... instead of j's, and the triplet legs (delr1 = xi-xj, delr2 = xk-xj, both measured from j) are formed with an unrelated k.
verified_by: orchestrator (the short lists are built per ilist slot at src/KOKKOS/pair_vashishta_kokkos.cpp:222-227 'd_neighbors_short_3body(ii,inside_3body) = j'; the FullB kernel takes i = d_ilist[ii] and jnum = d_numneigh_short_3body[ii] at :482-489, then switches to jj at :510-512. The local name j_jnum and the geometry both show the intent is j. This path is only reached with neighflag FULL, which the CPU-only CI does not exercise.)

summary: CommTiledKokkos::forward_comm_device(): in the generic (non comm_x_only, non ghost_velocity) branch the self-send case packs the buffer but never unpacks it, so the ghost atoms this rank sends to itself never receive their forward-communicated data.
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled with the KOKKOS device forward comm (package kokkos comm device, the GPU default) and either (a) an atom style whose forward comm is not x-only -- atom_style dipole (mu), spin (sp), dpd/react (dpdTheta,uCond,uMech,uChem) -- or (b) any atom style in a single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, where atomKK->k_x.NEED_TRANSFORM is true and even plain x takes this branch.  Whenever a rank is its own neighbour for a swap (sendself[iswap] != 0, normal with periodic boundaries and few tiles), the self ghosts keep the values from the last borders() call for the whole reneighbouring interval -> wrong forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->avecKK->unpack_comm_kokkos(recvnum[iswap][nrecv],firstrecv[iswap][nrecv],k_buf_send);' after the pack_comm_kokkos call in the sendself block, matching the ghost_velocity branch and CommTiled::forward_comm().

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 06)
summary: CommTiledKokkos::forward_comm_device(): in the generic (non x-only, non ghost-velocity) branch the sendself case packs the self buffer but never unpacks it, so ghost atoms a rank sends to itself never receive forward-communicated data.
evidence: comm_tiled_kokkos.cpp:233-237 'if (sendself[iswap]) { ...; n = atomKK->avecKK->pack_comm_kokkos(...); }' with no unpack; the ghost_velocity branch at 195-200 does pack_comm_vel_kokkos followed by unpack_comm_vel_kokkos, and CPU src/comm_tiled.cpp CommTiled::forward_comm() does pack_comm + unpack_comm for self. 'n' is assigned and unused.
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled with device forward comm on a GPU and an atom style whose forward comm is not x-only (dipole, spin, dpd) or any style in a single/mixed-precision build (NEED_TRANSFORM): with periodic boundaries and a rank that is its own neighbor, self ghosts keep stale values for the whole reneighbor interval -> silently wrong forces.
suggested_fix: Add atomKK->avecKK->unpack_comm_kokkos(recvnum[iswap][nrecv],firstrecv[iswap][nrecv],k_buf_send) after the pack in the sendself block.

summary: k_cutsq is marked host-modified only once inside allocate(), so cutoff values written to cutsq[][] by Pair::init() on a later run are never copied to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:1656-1658 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_cutsq,cutsq,ntypes+1,ntypes+1,"pair:cutsq"); d_cutsq = k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); k_cutsq.modify_host();' is the ONLY modify_host() on k_cutsq in the file ('grep -n "k_cutsq" src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp' -> lines 81, 153, 1656-1658). The only sync is compute() line 153 'k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>();', which is a no-op once the dirty flag has been cleared. PairExp6rxKokkos does not override init_one (see src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.h:90-94), unlike every other KOKKOS pair style in this package (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.cpp:338-339 'k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...; k_cutsq.modify_host();'), while src/pair.cpp Pair::init() rewrites cutsq[i][j] = cut*cut on the host before every run and src/DPD-REACT/pair_exp6_rx.cpp:722-728 lets pair_coeff set a per-pair cutoff.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style exp6/rx/kk 10.0 ...' / 'pair_coeff * * ... none 10.0' / 'run 100' / 'pair_coeff * * ... none 6.0' / 'run 100': the second run's kernels still test rsq against the old 10.0 cutoff (d_cutsq is stale) and also use the stale rCut in the shifted-potential terms, silently giving wrong energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Override init_one() in PairExp6rxKokkos to call PairExp6rx::init_one() and then k_cutsq.modify_host(), or simply call k_cutsq.modify_host() unconditionally in init_style()/setup() before the sync in compute().

summary: Roughly 690 lines of unreachable code follow an unconditional return in each of the two compute operator() overloads.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:399-412 is a block that dispatches to vectorized_operator<...> for all four (Site1EqSite2 x OneType) cases and ends with 'return;' at line 411; lines 414-753 (the whole original scalar kernel, including the a_f(i)/a_uCG[i] writeback at 748-752) can never execute. The same shape repeats at lines 772-785 ('return;' at 784) leaving lines 787-1133 dead. The dead copies still reference MathSpecialKokkos::powint (lines 581-1150) whereas the live vectorized_operator uses the local __powint<12> helper, so the two have already diverged.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today, but the dead kernels look like the authoritative implementation: a future fix applied there (as the powint/__powint divergence shows already happened in reverse) would silently have no effect on results.
suggested_fix: Delete lines 414-753 and 787-1133 so each operator() only contains the vectorized_operator dispatch.

summary: A misspelled guard macro (KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_simd, lowercase) permanently disables one of the three omp simd reduction pragmas in getMixingWeightsVect.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:2117 '#ifdef KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_simd' followed by '#pragma omp simd reduction(+:errorFlag1)', whereas the other two sites spell it correctly: line 1273 '#ifdef KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_SIMD' and line 2354 '#ifdef KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_SIMD'. Only those three occurrences exist in src/.
failure_scenario: The nTotal/fractionOFA reduction loop in the CPU-only (non-GPU) mixing-weight path is never vectorized; a silent performance loss only.
suggested_fix: Change the guard at line 2117 to KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_SIMD.

summary: The helper __powint uses a reserved double-underscore identifier and falls off the end of a non-void function when the compiler cannot fold the if.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:1138-1151 'template<int n> KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION KK_FLOAT __powint(const KK_FLOAT& x, const int) { static_assert(n == 12, ...); if (n == 12) { KK_FLOAT x3 = x*x*x; return x3*x3*x3*x3; } }' -- no return outside the if, and identifiers beginning with two underscores are reserved to the implementation in any scope (C++ [lex.name]).
failure_scenario: -Wreturn-type warnings (errors under -Werror) and a possible clash with a compiler/CUDA internal name; the unused second 'const int' parameter also makes call sites read as if the exponent were a runtime value.
suggested_fix: Rename it (e.g. powint12 in an anonymous namespace), drop the unused int parameter, and return the value unconditionally.

summary: pair exp6/rx/kk sets the k_cutsq host-modified flag only in allocate(), so cutsq changes made by a later Pair::init() are never pushed to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:1656-1658 (allocate()): `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_cutsq,cutsq,ntypes+1,ntypes+1,"pair:cutsq"); d_cutsq = k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); k_cutsq.modify_host();` -- the only `modify` on k_cutsq in the file.  The device copy is consumed every step: compute() line 153 `k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>();` and kernels at lines 497, 502, 504, 873, 878, 880, 1206, 1256.  There is no init_one() override (`grep -n '::init_one' pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp` is empty), so nothing re-claims the host write that Pair::init() performs on `cutsq[i][j]` at every run setup.  The robust idiom is the one used by the other pair styles, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:262, where modify_host() is called from init_one().
failure_scenario: Any command sequence that changes the pair cutoff between runs without re-running allocate() (a new pair_coeff / pair_modify that alters init_one's return value) leaves d_cutsq at the old value on a GPU, so the interaction range used on the device no longer matches the host bookkeeping.
suggested_fix: Add an init_one() override that calls PairExp6rx::init_one() and then `k_cutsq.modify_host()`, so the host write done by Pair::init() is claimed on every run setup.

summary: improper hybrid/kk keeps the base-class default centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL although every KOKKOS improper sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL, so the cvflag_atom accumulation loop dereferences a null sub-style cvatom pointer.
evidence: ImproperHybridKokkos::ImproperHybridKokkos (src/KOKKOS/improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:91-102) never touches centroidstressflag, so it inherits `centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL;` from Improper::Improper (src/improper.cpp:46). Every KOKKOS improper sub-style does the opposite, e.g. src/KOKKOS/improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:50 `centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL;` (same line in improper_class2_kokkos.cpp:48, improper_cossq_kokkos.cpp:50, improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:50, improper_distance_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_fourier_kokkos.cpp:46, improper_inversion_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_ring_kokkos.cpp:45, improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_umbrella_kokkos.cpp:46). Improper::ev_setup (src/improper.cpp:125-127) therefore sets cvflag_atom=1 (and allocates cvatom) for the hybrid but cvflag_atom=0 / vflag_atom=1 for each sub-style, leaving styles[m]->cvatom == nullptr (src/improper.cpp:44). The hybrid then runs `double **cvatom_substyle = styles[m]->cvatom;` and `cvatom[i][j] += cvatom_substyle[i][j];` (src/KOKKOS/improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:207-209). The guard in ComputeCentroidStressAtom (src/compute_centroid_stress_atom.cpp:189-191) only inspects force->improper->centroidstressflag, i.e. the hybrid's AVAIL value, so it does not catch this.
failure_scenario: improper_style hybrid/kk harmonic cvff + `compute centroid/stress/atom` (or `compute pressure ... virial` with VIRIAL_CENTROID, e.g. used by fix bocs / compute stress/mop-style consumers): the centroid check passes, cvflag_atom is set for the hybrid, and the first iteration of the accumulation loop segfaults on a null cvatom_substyle.
suggested_fix: Set `centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL;` in the ImproperHybridKokkos constructor (matching the sub-styles), or compute it in init_style() as the max over sub-styles' flags.

summary: Pair::special_lj is declared 'int special_lj[4]' (commented 'copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos'). Most KOKKOS pair styles shadow it with a KK_FLOAT member, but four do not - pair_gran_hooke_kokkos, pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos, pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos and pair_table_kokkos - so those styles truncate every fractional special-bonds weight (0.5 -> 0) and drop the pair entirely where the CPU style would scale it.
verified_by: orchestrator. Swept every src/KOKKOS/*.cpp that assigns force->special_lj into special_lj and checked its header for a floating-point shadow; exactly those four lack one (pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.h:89 is a correct example). pair_table_kokkos dispatches through PairComputeFunctor (pair_table_kokkos.cpp:150-174), whose factor is read at pair_kokkos.h:156/232 as 'c.special_lj[sbmask(j)]', so the truncated int is what reaches the kernel. Independently confirmed for pair_table by the group 28 reviewer, which additionally found pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:679 using a Few<int,4> for the same purpose.

summary: The /kk variant ignores atom->superellipsoid_flag and always derives the principal moments from bonus.shape, whereas the CPU style uses the pre-computed bonus_super inertia for superellipsoid particles; no guard rejects the unsupported case.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_erotate_asphere_kokkos.cpp:151-158 'auto shape = l_bonus(l_ellipsoid(i)).shape; ... inertia[0] = rmass*(shape[1]^2+shape[2]^2)/5.0' with no superellipsoid test, vs src/compute_erotate_asphere.cpp:114-127 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) { quat = ebonus_super[...].quat; inertia[0] = ebonus_super[...].inertia[0]; ... } else { ...shape based... }'. The sibling KOKKOS style guards explicitly: src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63-64 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot (yet) use superellipsoid particles with ...")'.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid superellipsoid' + 'compute e all erotate/asphere/kk' silently reports a rotational energy computed from an ellipsoid inertia formula (and from a bonus array the KOKKOS ellipsoid atom vec does not populate for superellipsoids) instead of the stored superellipsoid inertia.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) error->all(FLERR,...)' to ComputeERotateAsphereKokkos::init(), mirroring fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63.

summary: allocate_kokkos() grows k_a with DualView::resize() while both sides are in sync, which on a GPU build resizes the device view and re-creates a zero-initialized host mirror, silently wiping the coefficients of all previously defined dihedral types.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.cpp:345-351 `if (!allocated_kokkos) { k_a = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d(...,n+1,nterms_max); ... } else { k_a.resize(n+1,nterms_max); ... }`; coeff() (lines 364-380) then only re-fills rows ilo..ihi of `k_a.view_host()` and calls `k_a.modify_host()`, so rows outside that range come from the freshly created host mirror.  lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:1027-1030 `if (modified_flags(1) >= modified_flags(0)) resize_on_device(arg_prop);` and :962-973 resize_on_device -> resync_host() -> :1044 `h_view = create_mirror_view(typename t_host::memory_space(), d_view);` (a brand-new, zero-filled host allocation, no copy).  After a `run` the compute() `k_a.template sync<DeviceType>()` (line 96) makes both flags equal, so the very next coeff() that raises nterms_max takes the device branch.
failure_scenario: dihedral_style nharmonic/kk; dihedral_coeff 1 3 a0 a1 a2; run 100; dihedral_coeff 2 5 b0..b4  ->  nterms_max grows 3->5, k_a is resized on the device, the host mirror is replaced by zeros, only row 2 is refilled, and after the following sync<DeviceType>() type 1 has all-zero coefficients: zero dihedral energy and forces for type 1 with no warning.
suggested_fix: Do not rely on resize() to preserve data across the host/device split: after resizing, re-fill the whole host mirror from the CPU-side `a`/`nterms` arrays for all types 1..ndihedraltypes (as read_restart already does), or call k_a.sync_host()/modify_host() before resizing so the host branch is taken.

summary: The per-type-pair scale[i][j] prefactor of the CPU style is missing everywhere in the KOKKOS port, so 'fix adapt ... pair coul/long scale ...' is silently ignored with coul/long/kk.
evidence: src/KSPACE/pair_coul_long.cpp:121 'prefactor = qqrd2e * scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp * q[j] / r;', :131 'forcecoul = scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp * q[j] * table;', :134 and :155 all apply scale, and PairCoulLong::extract (:379-381) exposes it to fix adapt.  In src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_long_kokkos.cpp the corresponding lines :192 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = qqrd2e * qtmp*q[j]*rinv;', :178 'KK_FLOAT forcecoul = qtmp*q[j] * table;', :220 and :233 have no scale factor; 'grep -n scale src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_long_kokkos.{cpp,h}' returns nothing and params_coul (pair_coul_long_kokkos.h:48-56) holds only cut_coulsq.
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/long/kk plus 'fix adapt 1 pair coul/long scale 1 1 v_ramp': the CPU run ramps the Coulomb interaction, the /kk run keeps scale=1 forever and produces a different trajectory with no warning.
suggested_fix: Add a 'scale' member to params_coul, fill it in init_one from scale[i][j], and multiply prefactor/forcecoul/ecoul by it in both the table and the non-table branch (same fix needed in pair_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp).

summary: perform_pinned_copy separates two Kokkos::deep_copy statements with a comma operator instead of a semicolon in both branches.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_kokkos.h:275-276 and 280-281:
      Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),tmp_view,src.view_host()),
      Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),src.view_device(),tmp_view);
Both calls execute in order so behaviour is currently correct, but the comma makes the pair a single expression statement and will silently swallow the second call if the first is ever wrapped in a conditional.
failure_scenario: No current misbehaviour; a maintenance hazard and a compiler-warning source (-Wcomma).
suggested_fix: Replace the trailing commas with semicolons.

summary: The KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA (and SYCL) FFT-library fallback blocks forget to undefine FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL, unlike the HIP block, so a CUDA+NVPL build ends up with both NVPL and KISS defined and fails to compile instead of falling back to KISS.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fftdata_kokkos.h:43-55 (CUDA) undefines FFT_KOKKOS_FFTW, FFT_KOKKOS_FFTW3 and FFT_KOKKOS_MKL and then '#if !defined(FFT_KOKKOS_CUFFT) && !defined(FFT_KOKKOS_KISS) / #define FFT_KOKKOS_KISS'; the HIP block at lines 56-71 additionally does '# if defined(FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL)\n#  undef FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL\n# endif'.  The SYCL block (lines 72-84) also omits it.  With CUDA + -DFFT_KOKKOS_NVPL both FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL and FFT_KOKKOS_KISS are then defined: the typedef chain at lines 145-153 picks the fftw_complex FFT_KOKKOS_DATA, while line 268 still includes kissfft_kokkos.h, whose kernels use the '.re'/'.im' members of the KISS struct.
failure_scenario: 'make' with the traditional build (or any non-CMake configuration) using the Kokkos CUDA backend and -DFFT_KOKKOS_NVPL: a confusing compile error inside kissfft_kokkos.h instead of the intended silent fallback to KISS.  CMake blocks this combination (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:224-226 FATAL_ERROR), which is why it has not been seen.
suggested_fix: Add the '#if defined(FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL) / #undef FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL / #endif' stanza to the CUDA and SYCL blocks, matching the HIP block.

summary: Neither FixMinimize's nor FixMinimizeKokkos's destructor starts with the mandatory 'if (copymode) return;' guard.
evidence: src/fix_minimize.cpp:37-50 'FixMinimize::~FixMinimize() { atom->delete_callback(id,Atom::GROW); memory->destroy(peratom); if (vectors) {...} }' has no copymode test, and src/KOKKOS/fix_minimize_kokkos.cpp:101-105 'FixMinimizeKokkos::~FixMinimizeKokkos() { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_vectors,vectors); vectors = nullptr; }' has none either.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard as the first line of every base-class destructor a KOKKOS style inherits.
failure_scenario: Today the class is only used through lambdas that capture views, so copymode is never set and nothing double-frees; the moment anyone passes *this to a parallel_for the copy's destructor would delete_callback() and free k_vectors out from under the live fix.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first statement of both destructors.

summary: compute() never sets copymode = 1 around the pair_compute<> call, unlike every other KOKKOS pair style; the style-copy double-free is only avoided by the PairComputeFunctor destructor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_soft_kokkos.cpp:114-144 goes straight from `// loop over neighbors of my atoms` to `EV_FLOAT ev = pair_compute<...>(this,...)` with no `copymode = 1;`/`copymode = 0;` pair, whereas e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:107 and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp:125 set `copymode = 1;` before the call and reset it at the end. Safety today rests entirely on src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:103 `~PairComputeFunctor() {c.copymode = 1; list.copymode = 1;};`.
failure_scenario: Any future code path that copies the style object outside PairComputeFunctor (or an added Kokkos kernel taking *this) would run the copy's destructor with copymode == 0 and free k_eatom/k_vatom/k_cutsq/k_cut_ljsq that the original still owns.
suggested_fix: Add `copymode = 1;` before the pair_compute<> call and `copymode = 0;` at the end of compute(), matching the other lj/cut/* Kokkos styles.
